utterances.text: Yes. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What instruction was the Serbian Assembly of the ARK giving in respect of this referendum?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, in the first point here under this instruction, the ARK instructs assemblies of municipalities not to organise any activities regarding the conduct of this referendum. In the second point, it calls this vote for an independent and sovereign Bosnia unconstitutional and illegal because it was called by an unauthorized organ in violation of the decision -- or of the constitution by a decision of the rump assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina without Serbian deputies and therefore says that in all municipalities in which the SDS won the elections, the official organs of authorities shall have no obligations whatsoever to secure the premises on which the voting is supposed to take place. So this document essentially moves beyond asking for a non-vote or boycott by Serbian voters to the level of the municipalities' responsibility and relieves those municipalities of any obligation to conduct the voting.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, did the referendum subsequently take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The referendum was held as scheduled on the 29th of February and the 1st of March, and at that referendum, very few Serbs voted, and the overwhelming majority of voters, almost all of whom were Croats and Muslims, voted in favour of independence and sovereignty for Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: When was Bosnia-Herzegovina recognised by the international community as a sovereign state?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The European Community recognised Bosnia-Herzegovina on April 6, 1992. The United States followed the next day, April 7th, with that recognition. And that's the date -- the date of 6 April is normally used as date of recognition for Bosnia-Herzegovina's independence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I want to briefly go through the next series of documents, which is tabs 34 through to 38. So if you could have the first document in front of you, which is tab 34, Prosecutor's Exhibit 38, this is an extract of the minutes of the assembly of the ARK held on the 4th of March of 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. In this decision -- or in this meeting, on the second page of the document, we see there was an election of the executive council, or the president designated the executive council, and under point 3, the first of several decisions to assert authority over public functions within the ARK territory. Point 3 is, "The adoption of a decision to form the security services centre of the ARK, without debate." And on the next page, point 6, "The adoption of a decision to form the Krajina public enterprise for wholesale and retail trade in goods." And then on the fourth page of the document, turning the page over, point 9, 'The election and appointment of a director-general for payment transactions and financial supervision of the ARK.' If I may, I would just go to the next document, which is behind tab 35 and is Prosecutor's Exhibit 38.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 39, excuse me. The point 1 of this decision of the ARK on 11 April, 1992, was to transfer to the state ownership of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina the federal commodity reserves and commodity reserves of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. These reserves were much more substantial than in other systems that I was aware of and constituted a sort of major resource in the event of emergency situations. I'm with trepidation going to move over to --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I'll give you the exhibit numbers because there was some confusion yesterday at this point, but I think I have it correct. If you could go to the next document behind tab 36, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 40?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All right. This document, dated 15 April, 1992, which is nine days after the recognition of Bosnia-Herzegovina's independence, is directed from the president of the ARK Assembly, Vojo Kupresanin, to municipal assembly presidents, and he asks that -- "Hereby asks you to immediately take the following actions in your municipality: Number 1, activate the TO staff or Territorial Defence staff in your municipality." And then next to last, that four-line item, "Organise the effective protection of people, goods, organs of authority, electricity supply facilities, the PTT," which is the post office, "industrial facilities, radio relay and TV nodes and transmitters, health institutions, traffic and transportation facilities, and water supply." And finally, "Establish full coordination with the regular and reserve police forces."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And if you could go to the next document behind tab 37, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 41?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a document of 20 -- reflecting a session on 27 April, 1992, in which, under point 1, "The regulations of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina adopted prior to 7 April, 1992, which are in accordance with the constitution of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and are not contrary to the regulations adopted by the Assembly of the Serbian People at its sessions, shall be applied in the ARK." So this document establishes those -- this establishes as the authority for any laws, the constitution of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the sessions of the -- laws of the -- passed by the Assembly of the Serbian People.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And lastly in this series of documents, the document behind tab 38, Prosecutor's Exhibit 42, which is a series of conclusions of the Autonomous Region of Krajina from the 30th of June of 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document reflects results of a meeting on the 30th of June, 1992, of the executive council of the ARK, and point 1, "Government hereby guarantees the rights of all people regardless of their religious or ethnic affiliation who in these difficult times have expressed their patriotic inclination." That statement of rights of all, with the qualifier, those who have expressed their patriotic inclination, is a kind of qualification of those rights.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What patriotic inclination are they referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, one must assume that this refers to a patriotic inclination in support of the Serbian people --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I would object to what one must assume. He seems to have no basis for that kind of an answer. If he has a basis, let him establish it, but I would object to him just making assumptions, bold assumptions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Objection sustained. Actually, the conclusion is actually evident just the same, but the objection is sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, when an objection is raised, is it possible for me to actually speak to it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I think that Dr. Donia is perfectly entitled to make logical inferences from documents, and I think, quite frankly, it's absolutely clear what this document is referring to, and I think it's not unreasonable that he should come to that kind of conclusion based on what is actually stated in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley, it's an opinion, and it shouldn't be put as an opinion like that. Even though he is an expert witness, he should not comment on a statement which is contained in an official, or what is purported to be an official, statement like this, and should leave the Chamber to draw its conclusions, which, as you say, may be very obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, those documents taken together, Prosecutor's Exhibit 38 to 42, if you were to summarise the effects of those documents, what would you say to the Court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think the documents individually express the assertion of authority by the ARK over these individual institutions and aspects of public life of the ARK in the spheres of economics, economic life, military and institutions of transportation and communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: All of these aspects of life, what kind of indices are they, economy, military, transportation, communication?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They are the essential economic functions that, in this post -- early post-socialist period, were essential to the functioning of the state and society.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we can now move to the document behind tab 39, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 43, and these are the extract from the minutes of a meeting of the ARK Assembly held on the 17th of July of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Donia, what was significant about this meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This meeting was attended by several leaders from the Serbian Republic of Krajina, that is the Krajina located in Croatia, and military representatives from the Bosnian Serb Army, the VRS, as well as a couple of ministers from the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And as such, it was kind of a joint report to the ARK on the broadly military, political and security situation in both territories. And the reports submitted are identified under item 1, number 1, Mr. Radoslav Brdjanin, President of the War Presidency of the ARK, and Mr. Stojan Zupljanin, Secretary of the Secretariat of the Interior and Chief of the Security Services Centre of the ARK, submitted reports on the current political and security situation in the ARK. Also, Generals Momir Talic, Zivorad Ninkovic, and Minister of the Interior of the Serbian Republic of Krajina, Milan Martic, informed the assembly members of the military operations of the army of the VRS and the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the Posavina. There are then further reports indicated here from Mr. Velibor Ostojic and Mr. Bogdan Subotic, respectively Ministers in -- for Information and Defence. And then Mr. Goran Hadzic and Mr. Mirko Ljubicic, who was President of the municipality of Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could move to the next document, which is behind tab 40, it's a document dated the same date as the meeting took place in Banja Luka, 17th of July of 1992, Prosecutor's Exhibit 44. And this is a document from the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina to the Presidency of the Serbian republic and concerns the municipality of Bihac. Can you explain to the Court the significance of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was -- is dated 17 July 1992 and represents the decision of the ARK to appeal to the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina to liberate the town of Bihac so that it comprises an integral part of the Serbian republic. The rationale for this is that in the case that there was a majority Serbian population in Bihac municipality -- reading from the second paragraph here: "43.7 per cent of the population was Serbian, 35.5 Muslim, and the rest Croatian. In the wake of the genocide, this percentage was virtually halved, as it has been following the renewed expulsion of Serbs from a town in Bihac in this war." Bihac, it will be recalled, established a Serbian assembly immediately after the document of 19 December 1991, the instructions to the Serbian people. And it obviously -- at this point the final resort here of the ARK leadership -- ARK Assembly is to advocate its military inclusion or military conquest to include it in the Serbian republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, the word "liberate" is used. Who was the municipality being liberated from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was at that time under the military control of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the ABH.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we can now move to the next document, which is Tab 41, Prosecutor's Exhibit 45. And this is a public announcement of the Assembly of the ARK, dated the 22nd of April, 1992. What's the significance of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a -- really a public announcement that is addressed to the government of the Republic of Serbia, which is, of course, a neighbouring republic to Bosnia-Herzegovina. And just reading the -- from the first paragraph there: "Since the Serbian people in the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina is fighting for its biological survival and passing through the most difficult moments in its history, we request that the government of the Republic of Serbia return to the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina all able-bodied men between the age of 20 and 55 who have found refuge in Serbia so that together we can defend our homes from Muslim and Croatian paramilitary formations." Then: "If they do not accept the appeal of the Krajinan authorities, we will consider them the worst of traitors to their people" - that reference here is to those who have fled to Serbia - "and their right to return after the war and all their moveable and immovable property will be taken away from them."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could move to the next document, which is behind Tab 42, Prosecutor's Exhibit 46, a decision of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. What is the significance of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This decision of the crisis staff of 24 June 1992, signed by Mr. Radoslav Brdjanin, is a decision to check the conscripts of -- serving in military formations. And the first paragraph states: "The checks shall be carried out forthwith on all Croats and Muslims who have no declared place of abode or residence in the ARK." And two: "Checks shall been carried out forthwith on Serbian conscripts who have no declared place of abode or residence in the ARK and have not reported to the competent Secretariat for National Defence."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, previously, we've seen that the documents have been referring to an assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Now there is a reference to a crisis staff. Now, can you very briefly explain what had changed or what organs had developed, it's now being referred to as crisis staffs, within the region.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, crisis staffs for the municipality level, of course, had been directed from the SDS central board in its instructions of 19 December 1991. There was, however, no such instruction relative to the SAOs, the Serbian Autonomous Regions. There was, however, an appointment or designation of a crisis staff in the ARK prior to this document in kind of the spirit of other crisis staffs, which were essentially executive-type organs that would carry out the functions of assemblies in the inability or difficulty of the assembly meeting in wartime conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And we will have another witness who will address this in more detail, but broadly speaking, what powers did the crisis staff have at the autonomous region level of governance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't answer that question. I don't really know what the powers were.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, moving on to the next document, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 47, behind Tab 43. This again is a document signed by -- purportedly signed by Radoslav Brdjanin. What is the effect of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document, which is a -- reflects a crisis staff of the ARK decision, says that "No crisis staffs may be formed in firms." Now, the address form of the document to Autoprevoz, the Director and President of the Workers' Council, is such that the -- Autoprevoz was the place where some crisis staff had been formed. And he says: "Since you have not already done this and since you have appointed individuals for whom we have firm evidence that they are not for the policies of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, it would be best if you both submitted your irrevocable resignations." Now, this document rejects an alternative organisation of a crisis staff of the firm of Autoprevoz.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: We can now move on to the next document, which is behind Tab 44, Prosecutor's Exhibit 48, which is a public announcement signed by -- purportedly signed by Vojo Kupresanin. What is the effect of this announcement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This announcement, which is the -- done in the name of the Presidency of the ARK, "renounces the legitimacy of Nenad Kecmanovic and Mirko Pejanovic to represent the Serbian people in any capacity." Kecmanovic and Pejanovic were the two members of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina who had been designated to replace Biljana Plavsic and Nikola Koljevic subsequent to their resignation from the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina on 7 April, 1992. Both of these people had run in the elections of 1990 and had received -- they were down the list, in terms of having received votes, for those offices on the Presidency. So this effectively renounces their authority as members of the Presidency. And it then goes on to say: "The Serbian people is proud of its heroes to the same extent that it detests traitors and degenerates such as the two mentioned."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So in essence, these were two Serbs who continued to participate in the republican government in Sarajevo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. At this point, both of them were members of the Presidency -- Serbs who were a member of the Presidency as the two Serbian members on the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And they were being essentially proclaimed illegitimate people because they continued to participate in the central government in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you could now go to the next document, which is behind Tab 45, Prosecutor's Exhibit 49, which is a series of public announcements with a European Community Monitoring Mission cover sheet on the document. What is the significance of this series of documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In May of 1992, the SDS moved to define its strategic goals and also reach an agreement on the territory which it controlled. On 6 May, 1992, SDS president Karadzic and HDZ president Mate Boban met and reached an agreement, which was widely publicised, to divide much of the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina between their respective state formations or parties. This agreement was reached citing the ongoing efforts of the European Community and the conference on Yugoslavia to reach a peaceful solution to the Bosnian crisis. However, it was done without the participation of Muslim representatives and without the knowledge of the European -- or of the conference leader, Mr. Cutilliero. And the -- I have in front of me a fax message sheet. And on the opposite side of that page is a brief hand-written note dated "London, 7 May 1992," in which Mr. Jose Cutilliero writes to Mr. Colm Doyle and says: "Could you in your conference capacity try to elucidate with the principles the exact terms and meaning of their alleged agreement and Muslim views on the matter." So that makes clear that the EC mediator was not informed in advance or was not a part of these discussions. There were six points to this agreement. And going forward two pages is a -- an English translation. I would highlight only point three: "Both sides agree that in defining the borderline between the two constituent units in the area of Kupres as well as of Bosanska Posavina" -- and then certain municipalities are listed -- "account should be taken of the compactness of areas and communications." This is a reference to the importance of the corridor running between the eastern and western areas of lands under Serb control at that time and also to the -- the situation in the area of Kupres, where there was a highway that was maintained by one side but regularly shelled on the other. And just to note that under the provisions of this agreement, they also invoke and invite the European Community to mediate their dispute on the area south of Mostar. The significance of this document from the point of view of the two who agreed to it, or at least to the Serbian side, is reflected in -- by turning over yet one more page to the press release labelled "Serb and Croat Leaders Sign Peace Agreement." This was a press release prepared by the -- by Dr. Karadzic's public relations firm in London. And the third paragraph there states: "The agreement overturns the mandate of the Bosnian independence reference for self-determination for a Bosnian state." This refers to the referendum of the 29th of February and the 1st of March. "Instead the mandate will be reversed. Bosnia will be divided, and in its place, three separate states will be formed."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't know if you wish to break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As you wish, Mr. Cayley. If you prefer to break Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. now, we will pause now, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So we will resume at quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Call Dr. Donia in, please. Yes, Mr. Cayley?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Before the break, Dr. Donia, you referred us to Prosecutor's Exhibit 49, which is the public announcement of the agreement on partition of Bosnia-Herzegovina between the Croats and the Serbs. Is there any mention in these public announcements of the Muslim people in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, moving six days later, to Banja Luka, the 12th of May, 1992, this is behind tab 46, Prosecutor's Exhibit 50, and these are minutes of the 16th session of the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia-Herzegovina. You actually state - it's page 75 in your report - it's the 14th session, but no matter, it's a typographical error. It was, in fact, the 16th session of the Serbian people. Now, this document, these minutes, essentially reflect prior events that have taken place. If you can direct the Court to the sections in these minutes which are significant for what we are discussing at the moment? And I think the first reference you will find on page 13.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I might begin with a reference to the first -- actually first page, which is a -- starts with a heading of, "The Minutes," and then proceeds to list the agenda in 14 items, and the very, very brief conclusion of each of those 14 items. On page 4 is the statement that the audiotape recording of the session is an integral part of the minutes, and what follows on pages 5 through - who knows how long here - are, in fact, the -- a transcript of the audiotape recording of the session. At this meeting, the assembly adopted the strategic goals of the Serbian people and briefly discussed each one of them, spelled them out. It also completed the process of forming a Bosnian Serb Army or VRS, and appointed General Ratko Mladic as its first commander. And the bulk of the discussion at this session concerns issues raised in the enumeration of the six strategic objectives and includes long discussions by both Dr. Karadzic and General Mladic. The discussion of the strategic goals for the Serbian people begins on page 13. In the last full paragraph, the first goal is stated: "Separation from those who are our enemies and who have used every opportunity, especially in this century, to attack us, and who would continue with such practices if we were to continue to stay together in the same state." This goal, as seen in the sentence immediately above this paragraph, is stated in the more general sense as, "separation from the other two national communities or separation of states." Going on, on page 13, and just to identify the speaker here, this is Dr. Karadzic, "The second strategic goal it seems to me is a corridor between Semberija and Krajina." Now, this is the -- also drew reference in the agreement of 6 May in 1992 in Graz, the notion that there should be a corridor between the eastern area of Serb-held lands, which -- the northern part of which is Semberija and the Krajina, the western held portion. "That is something for which we may be forced to sacrifice something here and there, but it is of the utmost strategic importance for the Serbian people because it integrates the Serbian lands, not only of Serbian Bosnia and Herzegovina, but it integrates Serbian Bosnia and Herzegovina with Serbian Krajina" -- meaning Krajina in Croatia -- "and Serbian Krajina with Serbian Bosnia and Herzegovina and Serbia." So there's both a purpose of reuniting the Serbian lands within Bosnia and uniting the Serbian lands in Croatia and the Republic of Serbia. And on the next page, page 14, the first paragraph: "The third strategic goal is to establish a corridor in the Drina Valley, that is, elimination of the Drina as a border between our two worlds. We in our strategic interest and our living space are on both sides of the Drina." So this abolition of the Drina as a boundary is the third goal with the idea of creating a -- or a homogenous Serbian land.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And just to be absolutely clear, the Drina River was a boundary between which two countries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the Drina -- I wonder -- we need a map. But the Drina ran as a boundary in part between Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Republic of Serbia. The fourth strategic goal, on page 14: "The fourth strategic goal is the establishment on the Una and Neretva Rivers." That would define a very expansive area, running from Herzegovina up into the Krajina. The next paragraph: "The fifth strategic goal is the division of the city of Sarajevo into Serbian and Muslim parts and implementation of an effective state government in each of these two parts of the constitutive state." The sixth goal, then, is the -- "The sixth strategic goal is the access of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina to the sea." These were subsequently adopted by the Assembly as the Serbian goals -- or the goals of the Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, if I can now direct you to page 22 of these minutes and the transcript of what was said by deputy Dragan Kalinic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I mentioned, there was substantial discussion subsequent to the adoption of these goals of the position or attitude that the Serbian leadership should take on some of these key issues of Serbian goals. On page 22, Dr. -- Mr. Dragan Kalinic was speaking. And in the second paragraph of his speech, down about four lines: "Among all the issues this assembly should decide on, the most important one is this: Have we chosen the option of war or the option of negotiation? I say this with a reason, and I must instantly add that knowing who our enemies are, how perfidious they are, how they cannot be trusted until they are physically militarily destroyed and crushed, which of course implies eliminating and liquidating their key people, I do not hesitate in selecting the first option, the option of war, because I believe that our fate, the fate of Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I do not link it in any way to the fate of Serbia and Montenegro" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Our sentimental and national bonds" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Donia --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Slow down?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Our sentimental and national bonds must be reduced in this respect to a pragmatic level and established on the basis of interest that the fate of Serbs in BH cannot be resolved in any other way but by war." Mr. Kalinic's speech continues on page 24. It's all one paragraph. About two thirds of the way down the page, there is a -- the word "NO," both letters capitalised. Following that word: "However, those who will be planning the Sarajevo operation, either of liberating Sarajevo or of destroying the enemy forces in Sarajevo will have to plan what to do with the medical facilities. And let me tell you this right now, if the military hospital is to end up in the hands of the enemy, I am for the destruction of the Kosovo hospital so that the enemy has nowhere to go for medical help." Add at this point that Mr. Kalinic was the Minister of Health of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. On page 29, Mr. Radoslav Brdjanin begins to speak. At the bottom of the page: "Mr. President, I asked for the floor only after I realised that I was the most remote, that compared to everyone else, I am a kindergartner. I would first of all like to thank all those who -- all those participating in the discussion. I would like to say a heart-felt bravo to Mr. Kalinic. In all my appearances in this joint assembly, it has never crossed my mind that although he seems quiet while I seem hawkish, his opinions are the closest to mine. I believe that this is the formula, that we should adhere to this formula." After a further discussion on page 60, the draft decision on establishing the Serbian army of Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina army is considered, in the fourth full paragraph: "Pursuant to amendment 2 of the constitution of the Serbian Republic of BH and in conjunction with Article 70, item 2 of the constitution of SRBH, Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the national assembly hereby adopts the decision on establishing the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina army: "1: The Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina army is hereby established. "2: Existing Territorial Defence units and staffs shall hereby be renamed into commands and units of the army which will have its organisation and establishment determined by the president of the republic. "3: Lieutenant General Ratko Mladic is hereby appointed the Commander of the Main Staff of the Serbian Republic of BH army. "4: The Serbian Republic of the BH army shall wear uniforms and insignia of rank worn by the members of the JNA and Territorial Defence." With that, the Serbian army or VRS was established, and shortly thereafter, the session was adjourned.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Earlier, you referred to Mr. Kalinic and what he said at this meeting, and I just wanted to ensure that the transcript is correct, because the name is misspelled. I know the transcript is corrected afterwards, but the spelling of Mr. Kalinic's name is K-a-l-i-n-i-c?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Donia, if we can go now to the last document that I wish you to refer to, which is the document behind tab 48, you probably don't have a tab in your version but it's Prosecutor's Exhibit 52, which is the transcript of the 50th assembly -- the 50th session of the Assembly of Republika Srpska, and in English, there is an extract of a speech made by Dr. Karadzic, and I think the relevant part is at page 2. If you could summarise to the Court the significance of what was being stated by Dr. Karadzic in this part of his speech?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This part of Dr. Karadzic's address is a recollection of how the SDS organised life at the beginning of its existence from 1990 to 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Just to interrupt you, Dr. Donia, on what date did this meeting take place, can you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was -- it was April or May of 1995, so it was --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay, 15 April, 1995. I do not have the date in front of me. I see it's the fifth -- on the B/C/S, I see that it is the 15th and 16th of April of 1995, in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this discussion of the beginning years of the SDS and the Bosnian Serb Republic, he says, starting at line 2, "I want to say how it was. At the moment the war began, in the municipalities where we were in the majority" --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Slow down a little, because the interpreters can't follow you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. "... we had municipal power, held it firmly, controlled everything. In the municipalities where we were in the minority, we set up secret government, municipal boards, municipal assemblies, presidents of executive boards. You will remember, the A and B variants. In the B variant, where we were in the minority - 20 per cent, 15 per cent - we had set up a government and a brigade, a unit, no matter what size, but there was a detachment with a commander. The war began, and the JNA helped as much as it could here and there, it had helped before - I hope this will not be going out on HTV - General Subotic helped just before the war began by sending tanks." Then if I may move down to the section in which there are a number of -- a whole lot of names in upper case, about two-thirds of the way down. The sentence begins, "Gentlemen, we got the officers we asked for. I asked for Mladic. General Ninkovic, then a colonel, and General Perisic had visited me before that, and I had noticed Mladic's blunt statements in the newspapers. He was already in Knin then. I took an interest in him, and together with Mr. Krajisnik, I went to General Kukanjac's office and listened to him issuing orders and commanding around Kupres and Knin. We spent countless nights in the office of General Kukanjac at that time. President Krajisnik was already president of the assembly, and I was just the president of the party, I did not have any state function. We asked for Mladic and said that they should set up the headquarters as they saw fit, we wouldn't interfere." And then just skipping down six lines: "Later, we demobilised it, but the core of the army existed in every municipality. I would like to hear in which municipality it did not exist. With the arrival of the first active-duty officers, it could immediately be seen which active-duty officers were men of the people, ideologically not poisoned, and which were poisoned. Immediately, right away, those who were ideologically poisoned, who at that point lacked Serbhood, particularly orthodox faith, right away they knew that the Serbian government was no good, right away each municipality president was a thief and a fool." If I can just turn to page 4, the observations about the relations with the military continue on page 4, the first full paragraph, "What is the essence? The essence is what Djuric or someone said in the first speech - the army should blend into the state, Kupresanin. The army should blend into the state, become an organ of the state, not a repairman we hire or order, someone whose requests we have to fulfil, nor a structure which can place itself above everybody." The next paragraph, the last sentence -- next-to-last sentence: "It is clear, a commander obeys the supreme command, and all his assistants and corps commanders must obey him, et cetera. There can be no split in these organs, and if it is not running smoothly, if it is not going well, if it is not working like a clockwork, if it is running ..." et cetera. "So far, we have had a very active mutual relationship." There are a number of other comments in his speech about military-civilian relations within the government of the RS, which speak to some disagreements which were then being publicly discussed, but those are the essential comments on bringing the army into the authority of the civilian government.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, we've come to the end of this binder. We've come to the end of your report. You have, at the end of your report, a number of conclusions, which are really based on the consideration of both binders together, what these documents essentially say to us years later. Could you please provide to the Judges a summary of those conclusions contained in your report, the conclusions that you came to based on your consideration of all of these documents and your knowledge of the region and its peoples?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First, I would say that the political developments characterised by the word "regionalisation" transformed the political structure of Bosnia-Herzegovina well before April of 1992, and that process of regionalisation involved splitting up, redefining, restructuring municipalities, as well as the more evident, more obvious, process of forming regional associations of municipalities, such as the ARK. And therefore, the political foundation for a Serbian state was laid, in a sense, from the ground up. It was a process that began at the municipality level, sponsored by the highest levels of the SDS and levels in between. That process led to various institutions being created, and undergoing a number of name changes, from Crisis Staffs to War Presidencies and Serbian Assemblies and a number of other iterations of the same basic notion. I don't see a great deal of significance to these different titles that are ascribed or adopted by these bodies over time, for they all shared the single purpose of creating a Serbian-dominated state on Serbian-specified territory. I'm struck by how little -- how few references there are to non-Serbs in the deliberative minutes that I've looked at, almost as though they didn't exist. They are simply not entering into the narrative that is exercised in these deliberative bodies. There are occasional references to assuring the rights of members of other nationalities, and there are occasional references in these documents to the need to bring Serbs back from other territories into the areas of the Serbian state, but very, very little is said about non-Serbs. At the same time, perusing the population composition of the Republika Srpska in 1996 up to the present day, that has become -- that became, in the words of the Constitutional Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina, a nearly homogeneous Serbian territory. Certainly was that by 1996. Despite some modest returns of some non-Serbs to the RS, it remains largely homogeneous Serbian territory to this date. Finally, I would note that the regionalisation process, nearly from its inception had a -- as one of its objectives, the successful military mobilisation of a force, always styled as a defensive force. That process began in early 1991 when the JNA was a completely separate organisation, under a separate command, and by May of 1992, when the JNA had left behind or transferred to the VRS most of its heavy weapons and the vast majority of its personnel based in Bosnia, that transformation was completed and the Bosnian Serb Republic, the RS, had its military force in the form of the reconstituted or renamed JNA, known as the VRS. Those are the main conclusions I would outline from my review of this material and evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And indeed, the full conclusions are contained on pages 76 and 77 of your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I've now completed my examination-in-chief. I have spoken with Mr. Ackerman and with Ms. Fauveau, and they would like to commence their cross-examination tomorrow. I know I had made certain indications yesterday that I would bleed over into tomorrow. I finished more efficiently than I originally thought, so I'm perfectly happy for that to take place if you are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Actually, we are finished earlier and more efficiently, as you say, because the way you conducted your examination-in-chief was impeccable, and the Chamber is very appreciative of that, because that way, if we continue in this way, we will be able to move forward at a faster speed, and that is the wish and desire of all of us here. I also take it as very important to have the transcript of Dr. Donia's testimony today, particularly the conclusions, ready possibly first thing tomorrow morning. The conclusion, at least the part in which he draws the conclusions based on the rest of his testimony, I think is very important for the Chamber to have and for the Defence teams to have before they commence the cross-examination tomorrow. I think that should not present a big problem. More or less, it's already here. And I am making this statement meaning that the -- you will have the text in English, of course, which is the language of the witness. Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are -- because of the wonderful facilities provided here, we are able to make a immediate disk of today's proceedings and have it available to us immediately. There will be an official transcript, I suppose, in a day or so. But -- well, there's never an official transcript. To my knowledge, there has never been an official transcript in this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, there hasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: But there will be a better transcript in a day or two. But what we get from these machines is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So we will reconvene tomorrow morning at 9.00 in Courtroom I, not in this courtroom. And would you please inform the Chamber who will be starting with the cross-examination. Mr. Ackerman, I understand you --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, I will be starting at 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you anticipate your cross-examination to take how long from tomorrow's sitting?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I can only guess, and the best guess I can give you is it will take all day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All day. And Ms. Fauveau, would you anticipate that you will be in a position to conclude -- begin and conclude your cross-examination by the end of our work on Friday?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, certainly, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Merci. So I have put these questions again following up what -- the suggestion that you had made a day or two ago so that you can actually prepare for -- make the arrangements for Dr. Donia to return to the States.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Two housekeeping matters: The first one, you made an order yesterday that if exhibits are not translated into English, I think, within two weeks, they will not be admitted into evidence. This final document that we referred to, the fiftieth session of the Assembly of Republika Srpska, the version in Serbian, in Cyrillic, is over 200 pages in length. We rely only on, as I say, approximately -- well, there are 17 pages that are translated. Within two weeks, we are not going to get this translated, nor do we suggest to the Court that it should be, because quite frankly, much of it we do not rely on. Now, I'm sure Mr. Ackerman will turn and say, "Well, I need to know what it says." But if I submit this document to the translation department, I think -- I can't predict their reaction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can. Yes. Mr. Ackerman, I'll start with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a document from 1995, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And so it's unlikely --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 15th or 16th of --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It's unlikely that there is material in there that is relevant to a case that covers basically the year 1992. I can have my assistants here just skim through it and see if there's any other 1992 material there. If Mr. Cayley tried to use 1995 material, I'd be objecting, so chances are I don't have any objection whatsoever to it not being fully translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Ms. Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fortunately -- unfortunately, I think there may be other parts of this document that are relevant to this case and that refer to the year 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the position as it is being taken now by this Chamber for the present moment and until it has at least on a prima facie basis an indication of which other parts of that document could be of relevance to the -- to the case we have in front of us, restricts -- or rather, it does not extend the -- that part of yesterday's order to the remaining part of this last document -- we're talking of document P52B - 52B - since the Prosecution is basing and relying itself only on the part from Mr. -- Dr. Karadzic's statement or part of the speech, so the rest we will revisit if we need to later on, provided there is at least some prima facie indication to this Chamber that we need to. Otherwise it will remain as it is, and we should proceed with the -- with the part that has been translated, the remaining part or the remaining text in B/C/S remaining in its entirety as it is, without the need of having any further parts from it translated into English or French. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Unless the Defence identify --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, obviously, if there is. But we can't go on a fishing expedition. I mean, if we have an indication, yes, you will have all opportunities; we will even, if necessary, stop until we have it translated. But it -- the Chamber has to be convinced that there is the need for that. Otherwise, we will not entertain any -- any objections of those -- anyway, it's not an objection. It's a remark which Ms. Fauveau has made for the time being and the Chamber will reserve its position until and only if there is a clear indication that it ought to be -- ought to do so -- ought to change its ruling of yesterday. So that brings us to the -- is there something else?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: One last matter, Your Honour, a straightforward one. We provided to Your Honours a number of binders in respect of the Banja Luka municipality. If you remember, you decided that exhibits would, where possible, be pre-numbered in order to speed things up. Could we, please, ask for those binders back from Your Honours so that we can pre-number your sets, along with any other sets that were given out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. That will be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: No, that's fine. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are informed that the decision which was expected on the 92 bis has been handed down, and you should have already been provided with a copy. Okay. So the hearing is adjourned until tomorrow morning 9.00, to be reconvened in Chamber I -- Courtroom I. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
